steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: A joint is where two or more bones meet. Most joints in the body allow movement, and these are called synovial joints . | Hinge Joint: Allows movement in one plane only - flexion and extension. Like a door hinge, it opens and closes in one direction. | Ball-and-Socket Joint: Allows movement in all three planes - the rounded head of one bone fits into the cup-shaped socket of another. This allows the widest range of movement of any joint type. | Key Concept: The type of joint determines which movements are possible. Hinge joints only allow flexion and extension (sagittal plane). Ball-and-socket joints allow all types of movement including rotation and circumduction.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Name the six key structures of a synovial joint and state the function of each. | Compare the range of movement possible at a hinge joint and a ball-and-socket joint. | What is the difference between a tendon and a ligament?
